# Arrakis Security raises $8M Seed to secure enterprise AI agents

Arrakis Security raises $8M Seed to secure enterprise AI agents

What's the deal? Israeli cybersecurity startup Arrakis Security has raised $8 million in Seed funding to build a platform that monitors and governs the behaviour of enterprise AI agents. The round was led by Hetz Ventures, with backing from ElevenLabs chief executive officer Mati Staniszewski, Torq chief executive officer Ofer Smadari, Pentera founder and chief executive officer Amitai Ratzon, and several senior Palantir executives.

Who's behind it? Founders Tal Baron, Omer Efrat, and Ron Shani are veterans of Torq and Palantir. The company employs around 20 people. [...] Why now? Enterprises are rapidly deploying autonomous AI systems that access sensitive data and execute workflows without human supervision. Arrakis argues that traditional security tools, built for human users interacting with machines, cannot govern software that acts independently.

What's the endgame? The platform discovers AI agents across an organisation, builds behavioural profiles, and monitors activity in real time. When it detects suspicious actions — such as data exfiltration or privilege abuse — it can block them, revoke permissions, or suspend integrations. The new funding will expand its research, development, and product teams in Israel. [...] Ask anything about this entity

 Datadog CEO Olivier Pomel and OpenAI’s Olivier Godement invested their own money in the round, offering a rare show of support from top AI industry leaders instead of typical financial investors.

We’re excited to continue supporting Arrakis as it scales globally.”

Arrakis plans to use the new funding to triple its staff, improve its platform and security, and open offices in New York and the Middle East, along with its current locations in London and Paris. The company has already signed its first US customer and is seeing more demand in aerospace, energy, and logistics.
